newsitem.title: USA: U.S. police academy probed on anti-Semitism charge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. police academy probed on anti-Semitism charge.

text.p: Oregon Gov. John Kitzhaber has ordered an independent review into allegations of anti-Semitism at the state's main policy academy, officials said on Thursday.

A private consultant will investigate the academy after a part-time Jewish faculty member resigned over what she called a persistent anti-Semitic climate at the academy in Monmouth near the state capital of Salem.

Last summer, Sam Sachs, a Jewish sheriff's deputy from Multnomah County, which includes Portland, accused three academy instructors of taunting him with anti-Semitic remarks during a training programme, including comments about circumcision and taunts about Jews saluting Hitler.
After an investigation upheld the deputy's claims, one of the trainers resigned and the academy agreed to pay Sachs $50,000 to settle a lawsuit.

Last month, Maura Goodman, a Jewish probation officer and part-time faculty member at the academy since 1988, resigned saying there was a widespread bias problem at the institution, which trains 1,000 officers a year.
"There has been a persistent problem with bias toward women, as well as toward minorities and one of anti-Semitism," Goodman said in an interview.
She said her attorney was preparing a lawsuit against the academy and two instructors.
After the Sachs incident, the academy added a four-hour class in cultural sensitivity for trainees and hired a cultural consultant from the Jewish community.
But Bob Hornstein, community relations director at the Jewish Federation of Portland, said he was "very sceptical" that there had been changes at the academy.

"We have plenty of reason to believe it was not an isolated incident, that there is a pattern of behaviour directed not just against Jews, but against blacks, against women, against Native Americans, against minorities," he said.
Leslie Carlson, a spokeswoman for Kitzhaber, said Goodman's resignation moved the governor to take a closer look at the academy, which trains police officers in the state.
"I'd say it was definitely the trigger. He wants to get a good, clear independent look at what's going on there."
